metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: HTTP caching headers missing or misconfigured finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific implementation code, server configurations, and testing strategies to reduce server load, improve page load times, and minimize bandwidth usage by enabling browser and CDN caching for static and dynamic content.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your website has poor or missing caching configuration, forcing users to re-download unchanged resources on every visit, resulting in slow page loads, high server costs, and poor user experience.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: High risk of revenue loss through poor performance and excessive infrastructure costs. Without caching, every page view requires full resource downloads, creating 5-10x more server load and bandwidth usage. This increases hosting costs by $1000-$10,000/month for high-traffic sites. Users experience 2-4 second slower page loads on return visits (should be instant with caching). Each 1-second delay reduces conversions by 7% (Google). Return visitors (60-80% of traffic) get no speed benefit. Server capacity constraints limit scalability - need 5-10x more servers without caching. Poor Core Web Vitals harm SEO rankings. Competitors with proper caching gain significant performance advantage.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: Google Core Web Vitals requirements penalize poor caching. Web performance best practices mandate efficient caching strategies. No direct regulatory compliance, but essential for professional web applications and SaaS platforms.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing or misconfigured HTTP caching headers cause resources to be re-downloaded on every page view instead of being cached by browsers and CDNs. Proper caching reduces repeat page load times by 80-90%.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Should be addressed in current sprint. Implementation takes 2-4 hours including testing. Medium complexity - requires understanding different content types and appropriate cache durations. High priority for sites with return visitors or high traffic.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 2-4 hours for implementation and testing. Minimal code changes - primarily configuration. Low risk change with massive performance impact. Additional 2-3 hours for CDN integration if applicable.
dependencies: Access to web server or application configuration
Cache invalidation strategy for content updates

DEVELOPER.summary: HTTP caching headers (Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified, Expires) are missing or misconfigured, preventing browsers and CDNs from caching resources effectively, causing unnecessary re-downloads of unchanged content.
DEVELOPER.technical: HTTP caching uses response headers to control browser and CDN caching behavior. Key headers: Cache-Control (modern, flexible, recommended), Expires (legacy, specific date), ETag (content version tag for validation), Last-Modified (timestamp for validation). Cache-Control directives: max-age (cache duration in seconds), public (shareable by CDNs), private (user-specific, no CDN), no-cache (validate before use), no-store (never cache). Strategies: Immutable static assets (JS/CSS with hash filenames): Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable (1 year). Static images: Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000 (30 days). HTML pages: Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600 (1 hour) or no-cache with ETag. API responses: Cache-Control: private, max-age=300 (5 minutes) or no-cache. Cache validation: ETag (strong) uses content hash, Last-Modified (weak) uses timestamp. 304 Not Modified responses save bandwidth. Stale-while-revalidate allows serving stale content while updating. Cache busting: fingerprint filenames (app.a1b2c3.js) for assets, versioned API endpoints, query parameters (style.css?v=1.2).
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-525 (Use of Web Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information) - Improperly cached sensitive data can be exposed. Not caching is the opposite problem - performance degradation rather than security risk. However, lack of caching creates resource exhaustion vulnerability under load.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing caching configuration creates performance vulnerability through resource exhaustion and potential availability issues under load. Proper caching is defense-in-depth for availability and resilience.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-525 (Browser Cache Containing Sensitive Information) - primary concern is over-caching sensitive data. However, under-caching creates performance vulnerability leading to resource exhaustion. Without caching, application must serve 5-10x more requests, consuming server resources, bandwidth, and database connections. Under high load or DoS attack, lack of caching amplifies impact. Proper caching reduces attack surface by serving cached content instead of hitting origin servers.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Attacker exploits lack of caching to amplify resource exhaustion attacks. Every request hits origin servers instead of serving from cache. Repeated requests for same resources consume unnecessary server capacity. Combined with other vulnerabilities, creates availability risks. Not primary attack vector but contributes to system resilience. Proper caching improves availability under attack.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: LOW-MEDIUM - Primarily performance and availability concern. Main risk is degraded availability under load rather than direct exploit. However, critical for system resilience. Fix has minimal security downside if implemented correctly (avoid caching sensitive data). Recommended as defense-in-depth for availability.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Implement within 1-2 weeks. Medium complexity requiring careful configuration. Higher priority (immediate) if application has high traffic, return visitors, performance SLAs, or capacity constraints. Critical for CDN-enabled applications. Balance caching aggressiveness with content freshness requirements.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Web servers not configured with proper HTTP caching headers, causing browsers and CDNs to repeatedly fetch unchanged resources, creating 5-10x unnecessary server load and bandwidth consumption.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: Caching should be configured at multiple levels: CDN edge (CloudFront, Cloudflare - serves 80-95% of requests), browser cache (serves repeat visits), reverse proxy cache (Varnish, Nginx - optional), application cache (Redis, Memcached - for dynamic content). Cache headers set at: CDN response headers policy, load balancer, web server (Nginx, Apache), or application code. Different content types need different strategies: Static assets with fingerprints (app.a1b2c3.js): max-age=31536000, immutable. Static images/fonts: max-age=2592000 (30 days). HTML: max-age=3600 (1 hour) or no-cache with ETag. JSON APIs: private, max-age=300 (5 minutes). User-specific content: private, no-cache, ETag. Cache invalidation strategies: filename versioning (preferred), cache headers with shorter TTL, manual purge (CDN), stale-while-revalidate. Monitor cache hit ratio (target: 80-95%), cache size, eviction rate.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All infrastructure serving HTTP responses: CDN (CloudFront, Cloudflare, Fastly), load balancers (ALB, Nginx), web servers (Nginx, Apache, IIS), application servers. Must be consistent across environments but different cache durations per environment (prod: long, staging: short). Affects all HTTP responses. Consider mobile clients with limited bandwidth as primary beneficiaries.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Monitor CDN cache hit ratio (target: 80-95% for static content, 40-60% for dynamic). Track cache hit/miss/bypass metrics. Measure origin server load reduction (should see 70-90% reduction). Monitor stale content serving (should be rare). Alert on cache hit ratio drops below 70%. Monitor cache size and eviction rates. Track bandwidth savings (should see 60-80% reduction). Use CDN analytics dashboards. Monitor 304 Not Modified response rates for validation caching.

QA_TESTER.summary: Missing HTTP caching prevents validation that application delivers optimal performance for return visitors and prevents accurate performance testing of repeat page loads.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate caching optimization. Performance testing tools (Lighthouse, WebPageTest) flag missing cache headers as critical issue. Repeat page load testing shows no improvement (should be 80-90% faster with caching). After caching enabled, must test cache hit rates, validation behavior (304 responses), and content freshness. Browser DevTools Network tab shows cache status (from disk cache, from memory cache).
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Poor Lighthouse performance scores. Google PageSpeed Insights cache policy audit failures. Core Web Vitals non-compliance (LCP affected for repeat views). Excessive origin server load. High infrastructure costs. CDN ineffectiveness (CDN can't cache without proper headers). User complaints about slow repeat page loads. Return visitor abandonment. Wasted bandwidth. Scalability constraints.

generic.code:
# HTTP Caching Strategy Guide

## Content Type Cache Strategies

### 1. Static Assets with Fingerprints (app.a1b2c3.js)
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
# 1 year cache - safe because filename changes with content

### 2. Images and Fonts
Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000
# 30 days cache

### 3. HTML Pages
Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate
# 1 hour cache with revalidation

### 4. JSON APIs (Public Data)
Cache-Control: public, max-age=300
ETag: "abc123"
# 5 minutes cache with ETag validation

### 5. JSON APIs (User-Specific)
Cache-Control: private, no-cache
ETag: "xyz789"
# Private cache, always revalidate

### 6. Sensitive Data
Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate
Pragma: no-cache
Expires: 0
# Never cache

## Cache-Control Directives

public        - Shareable by CDNs and proxies
private       - User-specific, no CDN caching
max-age=N     - Cache for N seconds
no-cache      - Revalidate before use
no-store      - Never cache
immutable     - Content never changes
must-revalidate - Validate when stale
stale-while-revalidate=N - Serve stale while updating

## ETag Implementation

# Generate ETag from content hash
ETag: "md5-hash-of-content"

# Client sends on subsequent requests
If-None-Match: "md5-hash-of-content"

# Server responds with 304 if unchanged
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
ETag: "md5-hash-of-content"
generic.testCode:
# Test caching headers
curl -I https://your-domain.com/app.js

# Look for:
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000
ETag: "abc123"

# Test conditional request
curl -I -H 'If-None-Match: "abc123"' https://your-domain.com/app.js

# Should return:
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified

verificationSteps: 1. Test static assets: curl -I https://your-domain.com/static/app.js
2. Verify Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
3. Test images: verify max-age=2592000 (30 days)
4. Test HTML: verify shorter cache (1 hour)
5. Test API: verify ETag header present
6. Test conditional request: curl -H 'If-None-Match: etag' returns 304
7. Open DevTools Network tab - reload page
8. Verify resources show 'from disk cache' or 'from memory cache'
9. Check CDN cache hit ratio (should be 80-95%)
10. Run Lighthouse - verify caching audit passes

apache.config:
# Apache - Configure HTTP caching
# /etc/apache2/sites-available/your-site.conf

# Enable required modules:
# a2enmod expires
# a2enmod headers

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    
    # Enable ETag
    FileETag MTime Size
    
    <IfModule mod_expires.c>
        ExpiresActive On
        
        # Default: no cache
        ExpiresDefault "access plus 0 seconds"
        
        # HTML - short cache
        ExpiresByType text/html "access plus 1 hour"
        
        # CSS and JS with fingerprints - long cache
        ExpiresByType text/css "access plus 1 year"
        ExpiresByType application/javascript "access plus 1 year"
        ExpiresByType text/javascript "access plus 1 year"
        
        # Images - medium cache
        ExpiresByType image/jpeg "access plus 30 days"
        ExpiresByType image/png "access plus 30 days"
        ExpiresByType image/gif "access plus 30 days"
        ExpiresByType image/webp "access plus 30 days"
        ExpiresByType image/svg+xml "access plus 30 days"
        
        # Fonts - long cache
        ExpiresByType font/woff "access plus 1 year"
        ExpiresByType font/woff2 "access plus 1 year"
        
        # JSON - short cache
        ExpiresByType application/json "access plus 5 minutes"
    </IfModule>
    
    <IfModule mod_headers.c>
        # Add immutable for static assets
        <FilesMatch "\.(css|js)$">
            Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"
            Header set Vary "Accept-Encoding"
        </FilesMatch>
        
        # Images
        <FilesMatch "\.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|ico|svg|webp)$">
            Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=2592000"
        </FilesMatch>
        
        # HTML
        <FilesMatch "\.html$">
            Header set Cache-Control "public, max-age=3600, must-revalidate"
        </FilesMatch>
        
        # Sensitive locations - no cache
        <LocationMatch "/api/payment">
            Header set Cache-Control "no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate"
            Header set Pragma "no-cache"
            Header set Expires "0"
        </LocationMatch>
    </IfModule>
</VirtualHost>
apache.reload:
sudo a2enmod expires headers
sudo apachectl configtest
sudo systemctl reload apache2

aws-cloudfront.config:
# AWS CloudFront - Configure caching behavior

# Method 1: AWS Console
# 1. CloudFront > Distribution > Behaviors
# 2. Edit Default behavior
# 3. Set Cache Policy:
#    - Managed-CachingOptimized (recommended)
#    - Or create custom policy
# 4. Set Origin Request Policy if needed
# 5. Save and deploy

# Method 2: CloudFormation
Resources:
  CachePolicy:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::CachePolicy
    Properties:
      CachePolicyConfig:
        Name: CustomCachePolicy
        DefaultTTL: 86400        # 1 day
        MaxTTL: 31536000         # 1 year
        MinTTL: 0
        ParametersInCacheKeyAndForwardedToOrigin:
          EnableAcceptEncodingGzip: true
          EnableAcceptEncodingBrotli: true
          QueryStringsConfig:
            QueryStringBehavior: none
          HeadersConfig:
            HeaderBehavior: none
          CookiesConfig:
            CookieBehavior: none
  
  Distribution:
    Type: AWS::CloudFront::Distribution
    Properties:
      DistributionConfig:
        DefaultCacheBehavior:
          TargetOriginId: S3Origin
          ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
          CachePolicyId: !Ref CachePolicy
          Compress: true
        
        # Static assets behavior - long cache
        CacheBehaviors:
          - PathPattern: "static/*"
            TargetOriginId: S3Origin
            ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
            CachePolicyId: 658327ea-f89d-4fab-a63d-7e88639e58f6  # Managed-CachingOptimized
            Compress: true
          
          # API behavior - short cache
          - PathPattern: "api/*"
            TargetOriginId: APIOrigin
            ViewerProtocolPolicy: redirect-to-https
            CachePolicyId: 4135ea2d-6df8-44a3-9df3-4b5a84be39ad  # Managed-CachingDisabled
            OriginRequestPolicyId: 216adef6-5c7f-47e4-b989-5492eafa07d3  # Managed-AllViewer

# Method 3: Terraform
resource "aws_cloudfront_cache_policy" "custom" {
  name        = "custom-cache-policy"
  default_ttl = 86400
  max_ttl     = 31536000
  min_ttl     = 0
  
  parameters_in_cache_key_and_forwarded_to_origin {
    enable_accept_encoding_gzip   = true
    enable_accept_encoding_brotli = true
    
    query_strings_config {
      query_string_behavior = "none"
    }
    
    headers_config {
      header_behavior = "none"
    }
    
    cookies_config {
      cookie_behavior = "none"
    }
  }
}

resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "main" {
  default_cache_behavior {
    target_origin_id       = "S3Origin"
    viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https"
    cache_policy_id        = aws_cloudfront_cache_policy.custom.id
    compress               = true
  }
  
  # Additional behaviors for different paths...
}
aws-cloudfront.reload:
# Wait for CloudFront deployment (5-15 minutes)
aws cloudfront wait distribution-deployed --id DISTRIBUTION_ID

# Check cache policy
aws cloudfront get-cache-policy --id POLICY_ID
aws-cloudfront.verify:
# Test caching behavior
curl -I https://your-domain.com/static/app.js

# Check CloudFront headers:
# X-Cache: Hit from cloudfront (cached)
# X-Cache: Miss from cloudfront (not cached)

# View cache statistics
aws cloudfront get-distribution-statistics --id DIST_ID

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Backup configuration files before changes
2. Document current cache settings
3. If caching causes stale content issues:
   - Reduce cache TTL (max-age)
   - Add must-revalidate directive
   - Implement cache invalidation
4. For CDN: Purge/invalidate cache manually
5. For web server: Reduce expires times, reload config
6. Monitor for stale content complaints
7. Adjust cache strategy based on content update frequency
8. Can always disable caching entirely as last resort
9. Most issues are stale content - solution is invalidation, not disabling
verificationSteps: 1. Test static assets: curl -I https://domain.com/app.js | grep Cache-Control
2. Verify long cache (1 year) for fingerprinted assets
3. Test images: verify 30-day cache
4. Test HTML: verify short cache (1 hour)
5. Test API: verify private cache with ETag
6. Test conditional requests: should return 304 Not Modified
7. Open DevTools Network tab, reload page
8. Verify resources show cache status (from disk/memory cache)
9. Check CDN cache hit ratio (target: 80-95%)
10. Monitor origin server load (should drop 70-90%)
11. Run Lighthouse - caching audit should pass
12. Test cache invalidation works when content updates

manualTests.name: Verify Cache Headers Present
steps: 6. Check for ETag or Last-Modified headers
7. Test multiple resource types (HTML, CSS, JS, images)
8. Verify appropriate cache durations per content type
manualTests.expected: Cache-Control header present on all responses. Static assets have max-age=31536000. Images have max-age=2592000. HTML has shorter cache (1 hour). ETag present for APIs.

manualTests.name: Verify Browser Caching Works
steps: 3. Navigate to site - note load time and resource sizes
5. Check Size column for cached resources
6. Verify resources show 'from disk cache' or 'from memory cache'
8. Test hard reload (Ctrl+Shift+R) - should bypass cache
manualTests.expected: Second page load shows cached resources. Size column shows '(disk cache)' or '(memory cache)' instead of bytes. Load time 80-90% faster on repeat views. Hard reload re-fetches all resources.

manualTests.name: Test Conditional Requests (304 Not Modified)
steps: 1. Use curl or DevTools to capture ETag from API response
2. Make second request with If-None-Match header
4. Verify no response body sent (saves bandwidth)
7. Update content, verify 200 response with new content
manualTests.expected: Conditional requests return 304 Not Modified for unchanged content. Response includes ETag but no body. Changed content returns 200 with new ETag and full response body.

manualTests.name: CDN Cache Hit Ratio Test
steps: 3. Verify hit ratio > 80% for static content
7. Verify content updates after cache purge
manualTests.expected: CDN cache hit ratio 80-95% for static content. Cache miss rate < 20%. Resources with proper Cache-Control headers cached effectively. Cache purge works when content updated.

verificationSteps: 1. Clear browser cache completely
2. Navigate to site with DevTools Network tab open
3. Verify Cache-Control headers on all resources
4. Reload page - verify cached resources load instantly
5. Check resource Size column shows cache status
6. Test conditional requests return 304 Not Modified
7. Run Lighthouse audit - caching policy passes
8. Test CDN cache hit ratio (if applicable)
9. Verify sensitive data NOT cached
10. Monitor for 24 hours - verify no stale content issues
